items.statement: Over 12 months, at least 60 percent of eligible heart failure discharges from Hospital A are seen in the clinic within 14 days, with titration delivered as the protocol specifies in at least 80 percent of visits, and utilities and clinic costs can be collected within five minutes per visit.
items.rationale: Delivery must be known before value can be; the thresholds are what the finance committee would need to trust any later model.
items.risks: Spreadsheet data quality; the nurses' time limit.

items.statement: Ninety-day readmission or death is lower after Hospital A discharges than after Hospitals B and C discharges, after adjustment for age, severity and comorbidity.
items.rationale: A concurrent comparison is possible if the linked data arrive.
items.risks: Hospital differences unrelated to the clinic; the data office has not answered.

items.statement: A cost-utility model using published specialist-centre estimates gives a cost per QALY under the region's threshold.
items.rationale: Easy to compute but not credible for this service.
items.risks: Borrowed estimates presented as local evidence.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected because delivery must be established first.
